algorithms.name: A check run that did not judge the work
steps: When a pre-review run ends, take what ended it.
Merge conflict: send the task back to its builder as merge-needed, naming the files. Start no new run until the branch changes.
The Hub stopped: at the next start, request a new run for every task still waiting for its pre-review result.

Error of any other kind, or a check that ran out of time with no failing test of the task's own named: if the previous run on the same task work was not itself such a retry, request one run on the current main tip.
Otherwise (the retry ended the same way): request nothing more, put the run and its error on the operator's Needs-you list, and leave the task's status unchanged.
Any other failure: the task's own failure, as today (sent back as broken-check or flaky).

design:
D1 Merged commit by plumbing. The commit approval would produce is built with `git merge-tree --write-tree` and `commit-tree`, one target at a time onto the main tip, skipping targets already in the base. No branch, index or checkout moves, so building it is safe while agents and the operator work.

D2 Scratch worktree per task. The merged commit is checked out detached at `.agentweave/checks/<task_id>` under the project root (gitignored), with the repository's shared dependency directories symlinked in when the OS allows. It is removed after the run; a leftover locked registration is unlocked and force-removed before the next. Adding and removing it may take up to 900 s, since it writes the whole tree.

D3 One record per run (`task_check_runs`). Results are written after each check, so a reader sees progress. Deleting a task deletes its runs.

D4 Bounded, per-task queue. Two runs per Hub, one per task, in-process. A restart marks leftover `running` rows `interrupted` at startup.

D5 Never inside a request. Completion outside a turn, the end of a turn bound to a completed task, and an approval request with no current result each schedule a background run; the approval gate itself only reads (`project_checks.view`). Only callers that are approving may schedule.

D6 The gate asks only when the merge situation resolves (main branch set and existing, workspace resolvable, a repository), like the other what-would-merge gates. The override is the operator's alone, refused from any agent, and its reason is kept on the approval transition.

D8 Hub configuration stays in the Hub. A check's environment drops the Hub's own variables by prefix and by credential-shaped value, and output is scrubbed of anything removed, because check output is quoted to agents.

problem: A task can pass its own evidence and still break the project once merged onto a main branch that has moved. Running the project's own checks on main-plus-the-task's-work, before approval, catches that without trusting anything an agent says.

requirements.rationale: The Hub executes these commands, so only the operator may write them. A project with no checks (null or empty list) records no runs and approval ignores checks entirely.
requirements.statement: A project SHALL carry an ordered list of at most 20 checks, each with a non-blank name unique within the project, a non-blank shell command and a timeout of 10 to 3600 seconds (default 900), set only through the operator's project settings; no run credential SHALL be able to change it.

requirements.rationale: Work an agent completes mid-turn is only committed when its turn ends, so checking at completion would check the wrong commit. A check can take minutes; no transition waits for it.
requirements.statement: The Hub SHALL start a check run in the background, never inside the request that triggers it, when a task is moved to `completed` outside a turn and when a turn bound to a task that is `completed` ends. Requesting approval SHALL NOT start a run.

requirements.rationale: The record is what approval, the reviewer briefing and the operator read; a timed-out check left running would hold the scratch worktree and leak processes.
requirements.statement: A check run SHALL be recorded with the main tip it was built on, the merge targets, the merged commit, a state (`running`, `passed`, `failed`, `error` or `interrupted`) and, per check, its exit code, whether it timed out, its duration and the last 4000 characters of its combined output; a check that exits non-zero or exceeds its timeout SHALL fail the run, and a timed-out check SHALL have its whole process tree ended.

requirements.rationale: `error` is the Hub failing to check, not the work failing its checks, so it must not stand as a result the way `failed` does.
requirements.statement: When a merge target does not merge cleanly onto the main tip, or the Hub otherwise fails to produce a result, the run SHALL be recorded `error` with the reason, and an `error` result SHALL be treated as no verdict: it refuses nothing at approval.

requirements.rationale: A target already on main would re-check main and blame its failures on this task.
requirements.statement: Merge targets already reachable from the main tip SHALL be excluded from a run; a project with no main branch, or a task with nothing left to merge, SHALL record no run.

requirements.rationale: A restart kills in-flight checks; leaving them `running` would block approval forever, and a pass on an older main says nothing about the work approval would merge now.
requirements.statement: A Hub that starts and finds runs still `running` SHALL record them `interrupted`, and a result whose main tip or merge targets no longer match the current ones SHALL be treated as stale rather than trusted.

requirements.rationale: Checks are often whole test suites; unbounded parallel runs would starve the machine and the agents on it.
requirements.statement: No more than two check runs SHALL execute at once per Hub, at most one per task; a request for a task whose run is already executing SHALL start nothing new, and a request whose latest `passed` or `failed` result is current SHALL return that result instead of running again.

requirements.rationale: A check runs the project's commands, which may be changed by the very agents being checked; the Hub's credentials and database must not reach them or be echoed into records agents read.
requirements.statement: A check SHALL run with the Hub process's environment minus the Hub's own configuration: every variable whose name starts with `AW_`, `HUB_` or `AGENTWEAVE_`, `DATABASE_URL`, and any variable whose value starts with `aw_live_` or `aw_run_`; any removed value or credential-shaped string (`aw_live_…`, `aw_run_…`) appearing in its output SHALL be recorded as `[redacted]`.

requirements.rationale: When checks fail for a reason outside the work (a flaky test, a fixed environment), the operator needs to see why and re-run without touching the task.
requirements.statement: The operator SHALL be able to read a task's last 10 check runs, newest first, with whether checks are configured and whether a run is executing (`GET /tasks/{task_id}/checks`), and to start a run even over a current result (`POST /tasks/{task_id}/checks/run`); the task drawer SHALL show the latest run's state and offer that re-run.

requirements.rationale: A reviewer who does not know the checks failed approves into a refusal, or fixes the author's work itself.
requirements.statement: A reviewer's turn briefing SHALL state the task's recorded check result (passed, failed with the failing checks and output tail, could not run, or not finished) and that fixing a failure is the author's work, returned with `revision_needed`; reading it SHALL start no run.

requirements.rationale: Approval would otherwise land work that breaks the project. An errored run is the Hub failing to produce a result, not a verdict, so approving retries it (F516).
requirements.statement: In a project with checks configured, the Hub SHALL refuse a move to `approved` only for the task's own confirmed check failure on its current merge targets, whatever main tip that run was cut from, naming each failing check with its output tail. A missing, running, errored, interrupted or stale result SHALL refuse nothing and start nothing; a pass on any earlier main tip SHALL count; a failure on the project's known-failing list, or a flake, SHALL refuse nothing at any build level. What lands is decided by the landing batch's own check run.

requirements.rationale: The override covers a known failure the operator accepts, not an unknown, and it is an operator judgement recorded where the history can show it.
requirements.statement: The operator SHALL be able to approve over a failed or errored check result by giving a non-empty reason, which the approval transition keeps; any override reason sent by an agent SHALL be refused, and a running result SHALL NOT be overridable.

requirements.rationale: The sweep's only exit took four PATCHes.
requirements.statement: POST /tasks/{id}/land MUST accept an optional override_checks_reason and apply it as the approval PATCH does, recording it on the transition.
The task drawer's checks row MUST offer the task's earlier check runs, each with its state, time and every check's exit code and duration.

requirements.rationale: The operator lands work on master by hand; a refresh that fires only on the Hub's own merges would leave those stale.
requirements.statement: A main tip change made outside the Hub (an operator's own merge or push to the main branch) MUST trigger the same refresh within 120 seconds of the change.

requirements.rationale: The oldest waiting task is the one most likely to be approved next.
requirements.statement: Refresh runs SHOULD start in the order their tasks entered completed, oldest first, within the existing limit on concurrent runs.
The operator MAY give each check an optional list of path patterns, set in the project's Checks settings and refused from any run credential, as the rest of the check is.
A check with path patterns MUST be skipped when no file changed between the run's main tip and the merged commit matches any of them, and MUST run, as today, when one does or when it has no patterns.

A skipped check MUST be recorded in the run's results as skipped, with the reason that no changed file matched its paths, MUST count as passing at the gate, and MUST appear as skipped (no matching changes) wherever the run's checks are shown, never left out.

requirements.rationale: Replaces checks-run-in-the-background-on-the-work-approval-would-merg, whose 'every configured check' has been false since 31f77f2 (fail-fast) and ae3e151 (path-scoped checks). Stopping at the task's own failure is what made approvals stop waiting for checks that could not change the verdict; a failure main shares is not the task's, so it must not end the run early (operator, 2026-10-24).
requirements.statement: A check run SHALL execute the configured checks in order, in a Hub-owned scratch worktree detached at a commit whose tree is the project's main branch tip with every merge target of the task's approval merged in, and SHALL never run in the project's root checkout or an agent's worktree. It SHALL stop after the first check that fails on the merged work and passes on main; a check that fails on main too SHALL NOT stop it; a check skipped because no changed file matches its paths SHALL count as passing.

requirements.rationale: Replaces n2, whose state list predates `superseded` (ae3e151, migration 0143). A superseded run is one main moved past while it ran: recording it failed would blame the task for main moving.
requirements.statement: A check run SHALL be recorded with the main tip it was built on, the merge targets, the merged commit, a state (`running`, `passed`, `failed`, `error`, `interrupted` or `superseded`) and, per check, its exit code, whether it timed out, its duration and the last 4000 characters of its combined output, or that it was skipped and why; a check that exits non-zero or exceeds its timeout SHALL fail the run, and a timed-out check SHALL have its whole process tree ended.

requirements.rationale: The operator writes these patterns by hand, and a pattern that covers less than intended skips a check that should have run, with CI as the only backstop. `constraints-dev.txt` must not match `hub/constraints-dev.txt`, and `src/*.py` must not reach `src/x/a.py`.
requirements.statement: A check's path pattern SHALL match repository-relative paths as a glob in which `**` matches across directories, `*` and `?` match within one path segment, a pattern ending in `/` matches everything beneath that directory, and any other character matches only itself; a pattern with no wildcard SHALL match only the file at exactly that path.

requirements.rationale: A pass of the task's work counts on any main tip (approved-work-merges-in-batches FR-9), so the result is usable; ending it repeated the same work and cost about 8 hours of hub-tests in three days.
requirements.statement: A pre-review check run that is in progress when its project's main tip changes MUST run to completion and record its own outcome (passed, failed or error) against the main tip it was cut from; it MUST NOT be ended, recorded superseded, or replaced because of that change.

requirements.rationale: That run checks work that no longer exists; its result could never be used.
requirements.statement: A pre-review check run whose task's own work is replaced by a new completion MUST still be ended, recorded superseded, and replaced by a run on the new work.
A main tip change while a task's run is in progress MUST NOT start a second run for that task; the task has at most one run in progress at any time.

requirements.rationale: The failure may belong to the old main, which has since moved; before this change the run would have been replaced on the new tip, so this keeps that outcome for failures only.
requirements.statement: When a run cut from a main tip other than the current one ends failed, and its failure is not confirmed as the task's own, the Hub MUST start a run for the task on the current main tip without anyone requesting approval.
A run cut from an older tip that ends with a failure confirmed as the task's own MUST return the task to its author exactly as a failure on the current tip does, with no extra run started.

requirements.rationale: Many test runners can run only related tests if they are told the files; the list in a file fits any size of change and needs no shell quoting.
requirements.statement: A check may carry a command for a change containing `{changed_files}`; in a task's pre-review run, when the Hub knows the files the task changed, it runs that command instead of the check's command, with `{changed_files}` replaced by the path of a file listing each changed file once, one repository-relative path per line, both sides of a rename included.

requirements.rationale: A check is never narrowed on a guess, as it is never skipped on one (project_checks.py:224).
requirements.statement: When the Hub cannot tell which files a task changed, the pre-review run runs the check's command in full, and the result says it ran in full because the change was unknown.

requirements.rationale: Landing stays the full gate, and only a full run on main may take a test off the known-failing list.
requirements.statement: A landing batch's run, a run on main, and a confirmation or narrowing re-run never use the command for a change: they run the check's command or its re-run command exactly as a check without one.

A check result produced by the command for a change records that it was sized to the change and how many changed files it was given, and the task's check run shows it as sized to the change, with that count.

A failure from the command for a change is judged as any failure of that check is: failing tests are read from the check's report, confirmed with its re-run command, and set against the known-failing list.

requirements.rationale: The same tree with a different base changes which tests the command runs.
requirements.statement: A pass of the command for a change is reused only for a later run on the same tree with the same list of changed files; a pass of the full command is reused as today.

The project's check settings accept, save and return a check's command for a change, in the API and in the app's check settings; one that does not contain `{changed_files}` is refused on save with a reason naming the placeholder.

requirements.rationale: One list, read by every gate, replaces about 25 per-failure rules; a test is argued about once, when it goes on the list, not on every batch. Seeding keeps failures already being fixed from sending work back on the first day.
requirements.statement: Each project has one known-failing list. An entry names the check, the test's id (from the check's report) or the whole check when that check writes no report, its kind (fails on main, or flaky), when it was first and last seen failing, the run that added it, and its owner fix task. When the list ships, it holds an entry for each test named by a fix task still open at that moment.
A failing test whose confirmation re-run passes is added to the list as flaky, if it is not already on it, and is not held against the work that ran it.

requirements.rationale: Commits the Hub lands were tested as merged; a commit made outside the Hub was not, so main is checked once after it.
requirements.statement: A test that fails in a run on main's tree is added to the list as failing on main, if it is not already on it. Runs on main's tree are: a landed batch's own run; a full run of the project's checks, made whenever main moves by a commit the Hub did not land; and the narrow re-run below.

requirements.rationale: Catches main breaking with no commit (a changed dependency or environment), which would otherwise send every task back until someone noticed.
requirements.statement: When a test that is not on the list fails its confirmation re-run for one task and then, with no passing run of that test in between, for a different task, the Hub re-runs that test alone on main's tree once. If it fails there it is added as failing on main and is not held against either task; if it passes, both failures stand as the tasks' own.

requirements.rationale: Operator, 2026-11-06: a test comes off the list when it passes again. A flaky test passes most runs, so one pass cannot be the rule for it. A batch run stops at the first failure of its own (landing_queue.py:1353) and a narrowing probe runs only the failing ids, so many runs never run a listed test.
requirements.statement: A failing-on-main entry is removed when its test ran and passed in a run on main's tree; a run that did not run the test does not count. A flaky entry is removed when its test ran and passed in a run on main's tree after its fix task was approved, or when it has run and passed in 20 consecutive runs.

requirements.rationale: Operator, 2026-11-06. An entry without an owner is a quarantine nobody empties.
requirements.statement: When an entry is added, the Hub creates one fix task for it, naming the check, the test, the kind and the run that found it, unless an open fix task already names that test. The task is assigned to the developer of the loop or build the finding task belongs to; failing that, the finding task's builder, else its assignee; an entry found by a run on main has an unassigned fix task.

requirements.rationale: Operator, 2026-11-06: 'the user runs them later'. Today a task created assigned outside a flow is started for its assignee at once (hub/hub/api/v1/tasks.py:1064); this must not apply to these tasks.
requirements.statement: A fix task the Hub creates for an entry is not on any loop, flow or build, and no agent's turn starts on it until the operator starts it.
When an entry is removed because its test passes again, its fix task is left open and gains a note naming the commit of main where the test passed.

requirements.rationale: An entry with an owner task is the reason an override used to supply, so a Gated build need not stop for it (operator, 2026-11-06).
requirements.statement: The completion gate and the landing gate, for every build including Gated builds, treat a failing test that is on the list as not the work's. A failing test that is not on the list and whose confirmation re-run also fails is the work's. Apart from the narrow re-run above, neither gate runs a failure on a checkout of main to decide this. For a check that writes no report, an entry for the whole check means no failure of that check is held against work while it stands.

A landing batch is never held waiting for the operator. A batch whose only failures are on the list lands. A batch with failures of its own, or a check that timed out twice naming no failing test, is narrowed to the task whose part first fails or times out; that task is sent back to its author (with the reason 'timed out' for a timeout), and the rest land or are queued again.
A landing that went past failures on the list records which entries it went past, and the task's landing shows them.
The app shows the project's list, each entry with its check, test, kind, first and last seen, and a link to its owner fix task, in place of today's flaky-tests list.

The main-comparison re-run, the hold for a failure main shares and its release when main moves, the hold after repeated timeouts, the automatic override for shared failures, and the reconstruction of flaky tests from event logs are removed, and a test fails if any of them returns.

requirements.rationale: Operator, 2026-11-06. It governed the shared-failure override (requirement_gate.py:1212-1229) and fix-task filing (flaky_tests.py:409); FR-12 removes the first and FR-5 always files, so it would be a switch that does nothing.
requirements.statement: The project setting 'The Hub may override checks' no longer exists: the settings page has no switch for it, the project's settings neither show nor accept it, and saving the project's settings from the app keeps working.

requirements.rationale: Accepted evidence names the commits that approval merges and that the checks judge. The send-back is the finding that those commits fail. Left accepted, they stay what is checked, so no fix can ever be judged.
requirements.statement: When the project's checks send a task back (a failed check run at completion, or a failing landing batch), every piece of evidence that task itself recorded and that is accepted MUST become held, with the send-back's report as its reason, in the same transition that moves the task to revision_needed. The awaiting pieces are held as they are today.

requirements.rationale: The failure belongs to this task's unmerged work (F518). Another task's accepted evidence, or work already on main, is not what failed.
requirements.statement: A checks send-back MUST NOT change evidence recorded by another task, even against a requirement the two tasks share, and MUST NOT change evidence whose commit is already reachable from the main branch.

requirements.rationale: This is the outcome that was impossible twice on 2026-10-28/29: the check judged f7cf6d3 again on every completion of the archive task, and fd8aa77 again on the vault-tab task's (F1081).
requirements.statement: After a checks send-back of either kind, when the author commits a fix on the task's branch, records evidence at it and completes the task again, the completion check MUST run on the commit the review is given (that evidence's commit), and not on any commit the send-back held. When that check passes, the task MUST reach under_review.

requirements.rationale: The author and the next reviewer need to see that previously accepted work was returned and why. Otherwise the requirement looks like it lost its acceptance for no reason.
requirements.statement: The send-back's evidence note MUST name the requirements whose accepted evidence it held, separately from those whose awaiting evidence it held, together with the commit that accepted evidence was at.

requirements.rationale: Only the checks' send-back is the finding that accepted work fails. A reviewer judges what is awaiting them, and overturning a decision stays the operator's.
requirements.statement: A send-back by a reviewer (update_task to revision_needed or rejected, with or without failing_pieces) MUST continue to decide only the task's awaiting pieces, leaving accepted pieces accepted.

requirements.rationale: Approval only queues the landing; the landing can still send the task back. A flow that has already ended cannot pick that task up (F1080).
requirements.statement: A flow with stop_when_queue_empties MUST NOT end on an empty queue while any of its approved tasks has a landing in an open state (queued, checking, landing or held). It MUST end on its next firing once every approved task's landing has landed or the task has no landing.

requirements.rationale: A landing in progress is the Hub doing the work. Reporting it as a stall would repeat the false alarms F1049 removed for reviews about to start.
requirements.statement: A firing whose flow has no claimable work and whose only open work is approved tasks with a landing queued, checking or landing MUST be recorded as work in progress and MUST NOT raise a stall or wake the mender.

requirements.rationale: This is the outcome F1080 was missing: the send-back reaches an author who can act on it.
requirements.statement: When a landing batch sends back a task of a flow that is still open, the flow's next firing MUST resume that task on its assignee, as it resumes any revision_needed task.

requirements.rationale: On 2026-10-29 the F1083 task's completion check ran on the drive task's commit and reused a pass, so a change breaking two existing tests passed the gate. Retires F520's 'or by tasks already approved' (operator, 2026-10-29).
requirements.statement: The commits that a task's completion check, review turn and approval check treat as the task's work are the task's own: the newest commit on its branch and commits named by evidence it recorded. A commit named by evidence another task recorded, including against a requirement both tasks serve and including after that task is approved, never counts as this task's work.

requirements.rationale: The F1083 task's second and third completions recorded no check run at all.
requirements.statement: Every move of a task to completed, including each one after a send-back, either records a check run whose target contains that completion's newest branch commit, or says in the task's history why no check ran. It never skips silently because a stand-in commit is already on the main branch.

requirements.rationale: task-dac742f3f922 was sent back for lacking 00fe846, a commit of a task it does not depend on.
requirements.statement: The work a dependent task's checkout takes in from a prerequisite, and the work approval requires the dependent's branch to contain, are commits produced by that prerequisite task. A commit produced by a task the dependent does not depend on, directly or through its prerequisites, is never required.
A 'Bring in prerequisite work' commit made by the Hub names the task that produced the commit it merges.
The stall scan does not report a loop or flow as having made no progress while a run on one of its tasks is executing.

requirements.rationale: The mender reset task-799357e3e80e at 17:39 while DeveloperOpus's run was executing (17:02-18:02).
requirements.statement: Resetting a task (mend_reset_task, or any route that moves an in_progress task back to assigned or pending) while a run on that task is executing is refused. The refusal names the run, its agent and when it started, and the task is unchanged.

requirements.rationale: task-4161311000e6 was added during review with no assignee, builder or checker.
requirements.statement: A task added to a running build, by any agent or by an amendment, takes the build's default builder and checker unless the addition names them. The board shows each as 'by default' when it came that way.

requirements.rationale: Two send-backs on 2026-10-29, one a regression and one a merge only, both read just 'held (not named as failing)' in the history.
requirements.statement: Every move of a task to revision_needed records a reason class (defect, regression, broken-check, merge-needed, evidence-only or flaky) and a sentence of reason, whether or not it names failing pieces. The class and sentence appear in the task's history in the app and in task_history.

A reviewer's send-back without a reason class is refused, naming the classes. A send-back the Hub makes itself (checks or a landing batch) records broken-check, or flaky when a confirming re-run passed.

requirements.rationale: Opt-in: no project's gates change unless it chooses.
requirements.statement: Each check in a project's check settings carries a phase of review, landing or both. The operator can set it per check, and a check saved before this change reads and behaves as both.

A check whose phase is landing does not run in a task's pre-review check run. The task's checks show it as 'runs at landing', not as passed or skipped, and review and approval are not held waiting for it.
A check whose phase is review does not run in a landing batch's check run, and a landing batch is not held waiting for it.
Saving a check that is both fast and landing-only is refused with a message saying a fast check gates an agent's completion before review, so it cannot be landing-only.

While the project's 'checks give way to the user' setting is on, every process a check run starts, including the processes those start, runs at a scheduling priority below the priority of a normally started user application on the same machine.

requirements.rationale: Operator, 2026-11-04: no project's checks change speed without its say.
requirements.statement: The 'checks give way to the user' setting is off for every project until the operator turns it on, including projects that existed before this change. While it is off, check processes run at the priority they run at today.

requirements.rationale: All 13 error runs on this project were conflicts; re-running one on the same tips repeats it. The builder can resolve it; the operator chose the builder over themselves (2026-11-04).
requirements.statement: When a pre-review check run cannot merge the task's work onto the main branch, the task is sent back to its builder with reason class merge-needed and notes naming the conflicting files. No further check run starts for that task until its branch has new commits.

requirements.rationale: Deliberately replaces today's behaviour, recorded in vault fact fct-c1dfbea42f5e (an interrupted run waits for the next refresh or approval): nothing about the work was judged, so the task should not wait on an unrelated event to be checked.
requirements.statement: A check run ended because the Hub stopped is requested again when the Hub next starts, for every task still waiting for its pre-review result, without waiting for a main-branch move or an approval.

requirements.rationale: Deliberately replaces today's behaviour, recorded in vault fact fct-c1dfbea42f5e (an errored run waits for the next refresh or approval). Bounded at one retry so a project whose checks are long builds or paid time is not charged for a loop.
requirements.statement: A check run that ends in error for any reason other than a merge conflict is requested once more automatically on the current main tip. A second consecutive error on the same task work is not retried: it appears in the operator's Needs-you list with the error text and the task, and the task is not sent back to its builder.

requirements.rationale: Running out of time on a busy machine says nothing about the work; a named failing test does.
requirements.statement: A check that runs past its time limit, and whose output names no failing test as the task's own, does not count as the task's failure: it is retried and surfaced like a Hub fault (hub-fault-retried-once). A check whose output names failing tests that are not failing on main still counts as the task's failure, as today.
Beside each check's time limit, the check settings show how long that check usually takes: the median and the longest of its last 20 passing results in this project, or 'no passing runs yet'.

Each check in a project's check settings can carry an optional report path, relative to the directory the check runs in, naming the JUnit XML file the check writes, and an optional re-run command containing the placeholder {tests}. Both are set through the app's check settings and the project settings route. A check saved before this change, or without them, reads as having neither. A re-run command without {tests} is refused on save with a message naming the placeholder.

requirements.rationale: The report is the runner's own statement of what failed; console output differs per runner and per version, and the pytest summary was cut off or missing in exactly the cases that held batches. Classname and name are the two attributes every JUnit writer fills (Decision 5).
requirements.statement: When a check that names a report ends with a non-zero exit and the report exists and is valid JUnit XML, the failing tests recorded for that check are exactly the testcases in the report that carry a failure or error element. Each has a test id of the testcase's classname attribute, followed by '::' and its name attribute. When the testcase has a file attribute, the file is recorded alongside the id for display and for telling whether the build changed it; it is not part of the id. No test id is taken from the check's console output.

A test that fails in a check's full run and again in a re-run of only that test is recorded under the same test id in both, so the Hub matches it across runs, across tasks and against main. Two different testcases in one report never share an id unless their classname and name are both equal.

requirements.rationale: A re-run in the same directory as the full run (project_checks.py:1055, :1061) would otherwise read the full run's report as its own.
requirements.statement: Before every run of a check that names a report, full or re-run, the Hub removes any file at the report path, so only a report the run itself wrote is read. A failing check that names no report, or whose report is missing, empty or not valid JUnit XML when the check ends, is judged as a whole by its exit code and names no failing test. Its result in the task's checks and the build's caught list says which of 'no report configured', 'report missing' or 'report unreadable' applied.

requirements.rationale: Keeps today's meaning of a pass; pytest's exit 3 (internal error) and similar endings need no rule of their own.
requirements.statement: A check passes or fails by its exit code and time limit exactly as before this change. A report naming failures on a check that exited 0 does not fail it. A non-zero exit whose valid report names no failing testcase is a whole-check failure that names no test.

requirements.rationale: Windows' command interpreter refuses a command line over 8,191 characters.
requirements.statement: Wherever the Hub re-runs a check's failing tests (confirming a failure is real, comparing with main, narrowing a landing batch), it runs that check's re-run command with {tests} replaced by the failing test ids, each passed as a separate argument, and reads the re-run's report by the same rules. A check with no re-run command, or whose re-run command with the ids substituted would be longer than 8,000 characters, is re-run as a whole with its own command.

requirements.rationale: Operator, 2026-11-05: AgentWeave must be usable to build any type of project. Runner-specific parsing is what kept a non-Python check weaker and kept adding rules.
requirements.statement: The Hub's judgement of a check depends only on that check's settings, exit code, time limit and report. The Hub does not parse any test runner's console output for results and does not rewrite a check's command.

The check settings show the report path and re-run command for each check. They give a working example for pytest, Vitest or Jest, Node's built-in test runner, Go (gotestsum) and cargo-nextest. They say that test ids are the report's classname and name joined by '::', that a re-run command receives them as separate arguments, and that a check without a report is judged as a whole, with no per-test re-run or narrowing.

requirements.rationale: Which checks are cheap enough to make a builder wait for is a fact about the project's commands, so it belongs to the operator's configuration, beside paths and timeout. On :8000, ruff and black took 0.9-6.7 s and hub-tests 8-16 min on 2026-10-26/27.
requirements.statement: Each of a project's checks has a 'fast' setting that the operator sets in the app's project settings and through the project settings route. It defaults to off for every check saved before or without it. A check marked fast with a timeout over 120 seconds is refused with a reason naming the limit. A task's check run executes its fast checks before its other checks.

requirements.rationale: On 2026-10-27 T2's ruff failure was recorded 18 s after completion; the builder could have fixed it in the same turn instead of after a 5.5-minute review.
requirements.statement: When an agent moves its task to completed and the project has fast checks that apply to the work, the Hub first commits the agent's uncommitted work in the task's checkout to the task branch. It then runs the fast checks on the commit the task's review would be given, merged onto the main branch, before the completion is recorded.

requirements.rationale: An agent's only feedback on a refusal is that message (main.py:746-756, mcp_server.py:204-207); without the output it re-runs the check itself or guesses.
requirements.statement: When a fast check fails with a failure of the task's own, the completion is refused (409) and the task stays in_progress, held by its builder. The message the agent's update_task tool returns names each failing check, the commit checked and the check run, and quotes the check's output (its failure excerpt or the last 4000 characters).

requirements.rationale: Warn, don't gate: a builder must never be held by a slow machine. Under load a check checkout has taken over 60 s (F516).
requirements.statement: An agent's completion waits at most 120 seconds for the fast checks. When they have not decided within that time, the completion is recorded and the checks continue as part of the task's check run. A failure they find later returns the task to its builder like any other.

The fast checks run at completion are the start of the task's check run for that work. The remaining checks continue in the same run, and no fast check is executed a second time for the same merged tree.

requirements.rationale: Three reviews on 2026-10-26/27 ran beside a failing suite and found what the checks found. A deferral with nothing else claimable is reported as a stall today (scheduler.py:2685-2689, :4403-4410), and this wait lasts the suite's 8-16 minutes.
requirements.statement: A flow queues no review of a completed task while the task's check run for the work under review is running, has not started, or was superseded. The firing records the task as deferred, saying how long its checks have run and how long the previous run took. While that is all the flow is waiting on, the firing is not recorded as stalled and no loop_stalled stall is raised.

requirements.rationale: completed -> revision_needed is the operator's edge (task_transitions.py:134-141), so today only a reviewer's verdict returns such a task, which costs a review turn.
requirements.statement: When a task's check run ends failed with a failure of the task's own while the task is completed, the Hub moves the task to revision_needed, held by the agent that built it, and queues and starts no review of that work. The task's notes carry the failing checks, the commit and their output. The transition is recorded with origin 'checks' and a note naming the run, and the app's history attributes it to the project's checks, not to the operator.

requirements.rationale: A flow's tick is every 5 minutes, and a hand-off left to it waited about 2.5 minutes on average (flow_advance.py:3-6). The wait for checks must not add a tick's delay on top of the suite.
requirements.statement: When a completed flow task's check run passes, or ends with no failure of the task's own, the flow queues the task's review within 60 seconds, without waiting for its next scheduled tick.

requirements.rationale: Slice B lets any agent but the author take completed work into review outside a flow; without this, that path would review beside a failing suite as the flow did. The operator's explicit action stays theirs (warn, don't gate).
requirements.statement: Outside a flow, completion is gated and a failed task is returned as inside one. An agent cannot move a completed task to under_review, and the mender cannot hand it to a reviewer, while its check run is undecided or has failed with the task's own failure; the refusal states the run's state and how long it has run. The operator's own review dispatch is not refused.

The update_task tool's description says that moving a task to completed runs the project's fast checks on the committed work, can take up to two minutes, and is refused with their output when one fails.

requirements.rationale: Operator, 2026-11-05 (roadmap approval): a fast check is what an agent's completion waits on, so slowing it holds a running turn; on 2026-11-05 a starved ruff run timed out after passing.
requirements.statement: While the project's 'checks give way to the user' setting is on, every process a check marked fast starts, including the processes those start, runs at the same scheduling priority as it would with the setting off. Every process a check not marked fast starts runs below the priority of a normally started user application, as before.
The 'Checks give way to me' setting's description says that checks marked fast keep normal priority and only the other checks give way.

in_scope: Operator-only configuration of a project's checks
When a check run starts, what commit it runs on, where, and with what environment
How a run is recorded, read, re-run, interrupted, treated as stale and retried
What a reviewer's briefing says about the result
The check gate on approval and the operator's recorded override
non_goals: Running anything an agent supplies: every command comes from the operator's settings
The merge approval performs and the other approval refusals (conflicts, live turn, unaccepted evidence): approval-integration
The task status machine and who may approve: task-lifecycle-governance

summary: The operator configures shell commands (tests, linters) that the Hub runs, in the background, on the exact commit a task's approval would merge, and records the result. Approval is refused until the checks passed on the current main tip and merge targets, unless the operator approves over a failure with a recorded reason.
